name: Lena Olsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This interview is confidential. What does an ordinary day at the contact centre look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and lead the subscription and cancellation desk at our contact centre. My two-year college diploma helped with the account rules, but the hard part is hearing when a customer thinks a refund has already arrived. I am one of the stronger agents and earn about the normal rate. I use AI summaries now and then after other agents have tried them, then open the actual billing history before I approve anything.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is waiting for you after that shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Jo and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Jo drives a community shuttle, and we have around three months of expenses saved. Some similar centres are within a reasonable journey. I keep a notebook of cases that look closed but need one more call; I do not like making a customer repeat their story.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau feels like the little summary box we already have: useful for finding the date, unreliable for the money. I would keep the billing history open when an agent asks me to approve a cancellation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my desk remains steady and three months saved covers a normal household surprise. Jo’s shuttle shifts are fairly regular, but our mortgage still relies on both wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading cancellation disputes and checking the original payment line before signing a refund. In the first year of small change, I’d transfer the fee we no longer pay for a cancelled family streaming plan into our reserve each month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about work, attentive to the bill. A cancellation date is not the same thing as a refund date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which line would you teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a new agent the line where the next payment was taken after the cancellation. The AI summary found the cancellation but skipped the later charge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How did you choose the saving?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The children chose which streaming plan to drop with us. We kept one they use and put the other fee beside the mortgage savings.

say: I’d say **AI summaries** can find dates but need billing checks.
I’d keep **original payment lines** open before approving refunds.
think: I think my **desk stays steady** in AI Plateau.
I value our **three-month reserve**, although the mortgage still relies on both wages.
do: Keep **leading disputes** and checking original payment lines in 2026.
Drop one **streaming plan** and transfer the freed monthly fee to the mortgage reserve.
S0.quote: A cancellation date is not the same thing as a refund date.
fieldNote: She checks **subscription dates** against the actual money movement before she approves a customer refund.
The **three-month cushion** gives her room for a household repair without borrowing.
The family chooses a **small recurring saving** together rather than dropping every shared treat.

steps.text: Keep leading cancellation disputes and check original payment lines before refunds
Save the cancelled streaming fee each month for mortgage reserve
Drop one family streaming plan while keeping the one the children use

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will send routine cancellations through software, but missing refunds will still reach someone’s phone. I would ask for the new paid rota and a count of customers who call back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my team could lose hours even if the difficult cases remain. Three months saved lets us compare jobs, but I do not want to use it to subsidise a lower wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d learn the centre’s new cancellation AI on a paid shift by checking twelve old cases against the payment ledger. In the first year routine chats move, I’d ask my team to jointly request written paid appeal hours and call-back counts; I’d apply for a posted paid billing role nearby only if written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage after travel, keeping this desk until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with enough time to check the mistake rate. A missing refund does not become cheaper because fewer people are paid to hear about it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old case would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would include the case with a cancellation on Friday and a payment taken Monday. The date looked right until I followed the money one line further.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you compare another role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would subtract the extra journey from the weekly offer and check the school pickup with Jo (my partner). A neat hourly rate does not cover a late-care bill.

say: I’d warn that **routine cancellations** may move before refund errors stop.
I’d ask for **paid appeal hours** and call-back counts.
think: I think my **team hours** might shrink despite hard cases.
I will not spend **three months saved** to support a lower wage.
do: Learn **cancellation AI** with twelve old cases against the ledger on paid time in 2026.
Join the **team demand** for written paid appeal hours and customer call-back counts.
Seek **posted billing work** nearby only with written mortgage-covering net pay/hours and school pickup; stay until signed offer.
S1.quote: A missing refund does not become cheaper because fewer people are paid to hear about it.
fieldNote: She tests **old payment cases** rather than an AI demonstration.

steps.text: Learn new cancellation AI on paid shift by checking twelve old cases against ledger

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 could cancel a plan and settle the complaint without an agent seeing the missing refund. I would ask for written staffing dates and paid appeal roles before trusting the new route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the software could take most of my team’s paid calls in 2028. Robots around 2031 are later and do not change the first risk to a billing screen; our three-month reserve would run down fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d postpone the planned replacement of our reliable car and keep the cash for bills, provided it remains safe for the school run. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid accounts role only if written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage after travel and fit school pickup, staying at the centre until a signed offer; I’d take a required accounts course only if funded on paid time for that vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, because the speed of it is close to the size of our savings. Three months of expenses cannot buy a new profession on its own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How safe is the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the mechanic whether the car is safe for another year. If it is not, we fix the fault before we think about saving the replacement money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must the course connect to?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want the actual posting, the wage, the first rota and the training hours. A course without a paid opening is a cost, not a plan.

say: I’d warn **2028 AGI** may hide a missing refund without a paid agent.
I’d ask for **written staffing dates** and paid appeal roles.
think: I think my **team calls** could shrink sharply in 2028.
I know **three months saved** cannot fund a new career alone.
do: Postpone the **car replacement** in 2026 only if a mechanic confirms it stays safe for school trips.
Apply for **posted accounts work** after 2028 only with written mortgage-covering net pay/hours and school pickup; stay until signed offer.
Take a **required accounts course** only if funded on paid time for that posted paid vacancy.
S2.quote: Three months of expenses cannot buy a new profession on its own.
fieldNote: She locates the work risk at **2028 thinking AI**.
The **car delay** depends on safety for the school run.
The new role needs **net pay and hours** plus a funded required course.

steps.text: Postpone car replacement only if mechanic confirms safe school travel; repair unsafe faults
Apply for posted accounts job; require written mortgage-covering net pay/hours, school pickup and signed offer
Take required funded accounts course on paid time only for posted paid vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives time to find out which account-review jobs have an actual payroll line. I would ask the centre for a posted role and funded study hours together, not a glossy course list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn account review over five years if the job is really offered, though full AGI might check the ledger too. Jo and I can save more while I still have a steady rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded account-review course on paid time only if a posted paid vacancy requires it, and save a fixed amount each payday. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage after travel and fit the children’s pickup, keeping my current job until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can ask for actual numbers before changing desks. I need a posted wage, not just a course timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want to correct three mistaken refunds in a practice ledger during the course. If I only learn where the buttons are, I will still need someone else to judge the payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the family compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Jo (my partner) and I would compare the new journey and school pickup on the same calendar. A late shift could add care costs that eat the pay rise.

say: I’d ask for a **posted review role** before enrolling.
I’d ask for **funded paid-time study** beside the wage.
think: I think I could learn **account review** for a real job.
I know **full AGI** may do ledger checks too.
do: Take required **funded paid-time review training** only for a posted paid vacancy; save a fixed amount each payday.
Apply for **posted review work** after 2031 only with written mortgage-covering net pay/hours and school pickup; stay until signed offer.
Compare **journey and school pickup** with Jo on one calendar, including any extra late-care costs before accepting.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to inspect real terms.
S3.quote: I need a posted wage, not just a course timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us time to demand that a disputed refund always has a paid route back to a person. I would join my team in asking management for written appeal hours each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can keep the desk and add to our reserve for years, although cheap thinking AI could still take cancellations in 2036. Robots around 2039 come later and do not keep my headset paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep handling hard cancellations, save a fixed amount each payday and join the team’s annual demand for paid appeal hours. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid billing work only if my hours fall and its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage after travel and fit school pickup, staying until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the end of the decade, calm enough now to plan. A decade of warning before AGI is useful only while the wages keep arriving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the team compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the team to put reopened refund cases beside paid appeal hours. If both move in the wrong direction, management can see the cost of the cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children at their school unless Jo (my partner) and I had a signed offer with enough net pay after housing and travel. Some similar centres nearby mean we can look without moving first.

I’d defend a **human refund route** for customers.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could settle a cancellation before anyone notices the refund went missing. Three months saved is useful, but a long gap in my pay would hit the mortgage. I would need written notice, posted paid work with weekly wage and hours that cover the mortgage after travel, and funded training on paid time if that vacancy requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who calls back after an automatic cancellation takes the next payment anyway. Someone needs paid time and permission to refund a payment wrongly taken after cancellation.

headlineQuote: Someone needs paid time and permission to refund a payment wrongly taken after cancellation.
portrait: At **43**, Lena leads cancellation disputes after a two-year college diploma on typical pay.
She and Jo support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with three months saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** but checks the actual billing history.
She tests **new AI** on paid time and compares vacancies after travel costs.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could hide missing refunds while her paid cancellation work shrinks.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted mortgage-covering work after travel and funded paid-time required training would help.
